w: Swamishri and Shri Ashok Bhatt, Health Minister of Gujarat, inaugurated with Vedic rites the bronze images of Shastriji Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj in the vestibule of ‘Pramukh Swami Medical College’ in Karamsad.
In the morning and evening, Swamishri was engaged in meetings on the BAPS earthquake relief work.

In the afternoon while Swamishri was having lunch, the kishores sang the thal and recited passages from the Vachanamrut, Bhaktachintamani, Swamini Vato, etc. Swamishri explained and elaborated upon what each one of them said.
From 2.00 pm to 4.00 pm, a special women's convention was held in the mandir hall. The program included speeches by women and cultural programs by balikas and kishoris.
In the evening assembly, balaks and kishores impressively performed the ballet called 'Bhakta Prahlad'.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj had finished his puja and was going towards his residence. Meanwhile a volunteer said to Swamishri, "Gunatitanand Swami has said that if the great one casts even a slight glance, faults such as lust do not trouble one. So please cast your glance on us."
Swamishri said, "We have the refuge of God and we belong to Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj, so we will surely be carried across."

ds.t: The boat will reach the shore
w: Swamishri was returning to his residence after puja. On the way a volunteer said to Swamishri, "Gunatitanand Swami has said that if the great one casts even a little glance, faults like lust do not trouble us. So please cast your glance on us."
Swamishri said, "We have God's refuge, and we belong to Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj, so our boat will reach the far shore."
Today it was colder than usual. So, with the coming programmes in mind, the attendant sadhus said, "What will it be like in Jalandhar and Abu?"
Then the attendant sadhu expressed a wish: "May the cold not come, may it go away."
Swamishri, Mahant Swami Maharaj, said quickly, "No, no... why?"
The attendant sadhu realised what he meant, so correcting himself he put it again: "Then may the cold go away just for the time you are there."

Swamishri refused that too, saying, "Then what will happen to the wheat, the mangoes, the chickpeas and so on? We just need to put on two more blankets, that's all... Why spoil things for everyone for the sake of one?"
"In the good of others lies our good, in the joy of others lies our joy." Today everyone saw this life principle of Pramukh Swami Maharaj vividly in Swamishri.

st.t: Sikkim Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang ‘Felt Very Stress-Free and at Peace’ by Visit to Swaminarayan Akshardham
w: Sikkim Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang and family visited Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi. Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang along with family and Sikkim State Minister Arun Upreti offer puja to Shri Neelkanth Varni Maharaj at Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi. Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang and family performs abhishek to Shri Neelkanth Varni Maharaj and prayers of peace at Swaminarayan Akshardham, New Delhi. Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang traditionally welcomed at Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi by Divyamurti Swami Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang and Sikkim Minister of Urban & Housing Development, Food & Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Arun Upreti visited Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi.

Sikkim Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang, along with his family and Sikkim Minister of Urban & Housing Development, Food & Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Arun Upreti, visited Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi.
Chief Minister Tamang was traditionally greeted by senior swamijis on behalf of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.

The Chief Minister and his family offered their respects at the Swaminarayan Akshardham Mandir and performed abhishek of Shri Neelkanth Varni. They experienced the Neelkanth Darshan – a Giant Screen film on the epic journey of Neelkanth Varni throughout India, the educational Sanskruti Vihar boat ride through India’s 10,000-year heritage and contributions to society and also the Sahaj Anand Water Show that depicts a timeless message from the Upanishads using modern technologies.
Regarding his visit to Akshardham, Chief Minister Tamang noted, “It was a great opportunity for me to visit this place. I felt very stress-free and at peace.”
